Carbazoles from the [4C ++ 2C] Reaction of 2,3-Allenols with
Indoles
Binjie Guo,X in Huang, Chunling Fu, and Shengming Ma*[a]
Abstract: Am ild and efficient method using readily avail-
able 1-aryl-2,3-allenolsa nd unprotected-N indoles,A u +
-catalyzed cyclization,a nd aromatization to afford the final
[4C + 2C] products,c arbazoles 4, with an excellent selec-
tivity,i sr eported. The reaction demonstrates excellent re-
gioselectivity and allows the N@Hu nit to undergo reactivi-
ty unprotected. Am echanism involving as piropolycyclic
intermediate has been proposed and synthetic application
is also demonstrated.
Tricyclic carbazole represents ak ey molecular motif that is
widespreadi np lants, and many of these compounds show
biological activities such as anti-oxidative, anti-bacterial, anti-
microbial, psychotropic, anti-histaminic, anti-inflammatory,a nd
antibiotic.[1] At the same time, carbazole derivatives are also
widely used as organic materials with special thermal,[2] elec-
trical,[3] optical,[4] electroluminescent,[5] hole-transporting, and
light-emitting properties.[6] The important potentialo ft hese
carbazole derivatives hasm ade them attractive targets foro r-
ganic synthesis.[7] Although there are an umber of useful syn-
thetic methods for the preparation of carbazoles,[8–10] there
remain some limitations such as lowy ields and regioselectivity,
poor atom economy,a nd harsh reactionc onditions. These
methods mostly involveN -protected indoles, which require ini-
tial protection and deprotection of the N-substituent. In fact,
to the best of our knowledge,t here are only very few records
describing the construction of N@Hc arbazole skeletons directly
from the N@Hi ndole with no chemical pre-modification to the
N@H( Scheme 1). Such examples include:a )t he reactions of in-
doles with symmetric hexan-2,5-dione catalyzed by montmori-
lonite K10 under microwavec onditions[11a] or p-toluenesulfonic
acid (p-TSA) under reflux provide carbazoles in yields of 86–
96 %o r4 4–76 %, respectively.[11b] Here, there remains an issue
of regioselectivity when unsymmetric 1,4-ketones are applied.
Other reports of N@H-carbazole synthesis are:b )t he reaction
of indole with two molecules of the same 1-chloro-4-vinylben-
zene under Pd/Cu catalysis followed by 6e-cyclization affords
2,3-bis(4-chlorophenyl)-9H-carbazole in a2 6% combined
yield;[12] and c) the reaction of indolew ith 3-methylpent-1-en-
4-yn-3-ol catalyzed by aR uc omplex produces 1,2-dimethyl-9H-
carbazole but in very low yield (15 %), and also with an issue
of regioselectivity.[13] In addition, Liang et al. reporteda ni solat-
ed example of 1-indol-3-yl-3-alkynol with ICl affording non-N-H
3-iodocarbzaole.[14] We envisioned to use differently substitut-
ed 2,3-allenols as the [4C] unit to reactw ith indoles,[15] which
may provide as traightforward route to carbazoles with av ery
decent diversity and regioselectiovity by considering the
unique C3 reactivity of indoles towards the C1 position of 2,3-
allenols. Here, we wish to report the realization of such ac on-
cept with the unprotected indoles[16] (Scheme 1).
We observed that the reactiono fN @Hi ndole 2a with 1-(p-
methoxy)phenyl-substituted 2,3-allenol 1a catalyzed by
TsOH·H2O( 5m ol %) afforded the 3-allenylated product 3a
(Table 1, entry 6). Other acids have also been screened, but
betterr esults were not obtained (Table 1, entries 1–5). Reduc-
ing the loading of the catalystl ed to al ower yield of 3a and
ar ecovery of the starting material 1a (Table 1, entries 7–9).
As we know,g old catalysis hasb een appliedt ot he non-N@
H-carbazole synthesis by cyclization and water-elimination of
differently substituted indolyl-substituted propargylic alco-
hols,[17] and in the reaction of 1-indolyl-substituted 2,3-allenols
via ag old carbene intermediate.[18, 19] Although no cyclization
occurred with AuCl(PPh3)i no ur system (Table 2, entry 1), we

To demonstrate the practicality of this method, ag ram scale
reactiono f 1a (1.3921 g, 6m mol) with 2a (1.0539 g, 9m mol)
was conducted to afford the correspondingp roduct 3a
(1.4958 g) in ay ield of 75 %. Subsequent cyclization and ar-
omatization of 3a (1.3231 g, 4m mol) with DDQ (1.0895 g,
4.8 mmol) afforded the corresponding product 5a
(1.0039 g) with ay ield of 76 %[ Eq. (3)].F urthermore, such
ar eaction may also be conducted without purification af-
fording 5a in a4 7% combined yield [Eq. (4)].
These alkoxy groups on the aryl ring allow further oppor-
tunity for subsequent synthetic elaboration. Further treat-
ment of 5a with BBr3 in CH2Cl2 followed by esterification

lowed by intramolecular attack of the indolyl C3 furnished spi-
rocyclic species IM2,b ased on the detection of both 4a /4a ’
(see Table 2).[23, 24] Subsequent 1,2-alkyl migration/proto-deme-
talation sequence affords dihydrocarbazole 4a (path a) and
4a ’ (path b). By fine tuning the reaction parameters, excellent
selectivity of 4 and 4’ has been achieved.
In conclusion, we have developed av ery mild ande fficient
methodu sing readily available 1-aryl-2,3-allenols[25] and N-non-
protected indoles by aF riedel–Crafts-type C@Cb ond forma-
tion, Au +/Ag +-catalyzedc yclization, 1,2-carbon shift, and aro-
matization to afford the final [4C + 2C]-products, N@Hc arba-
zoles. Ther eactiond emonstratese xcellent regioselectivity
through the installation of specific substituents at the different
locationso ft he newly formed benzene ring in the indoles by
utilizing the substituent-loadingc apability of 1-(electron-rich
aryl)-2,3-allenols. The unprotectedn ature of the N@Hu nit
leaves further opportunity for further purpose-directed
modification. The application of the method for organic
synthesis, materials science, and bio-screening are being
carried out in our laboratory.
